title: Context-aware sampling and runner isolation for stable profile generation
creator: Nadia Chen
description: Improve the benchmark harness to produce deterministic, production-representative performance profiles during model onboarding. This ticket targets three areas: (1) context-aware dataset sampling to preserve token/sequence-length distributions and conversational prefixes, (2) stronger isolation and sandboxing for eval runners to remove cross-run interference (CPU/GPU shared state, seeded RNG leaks), and (3) metadata capture for each run to enable reproducible profile publishing and rollbacks. The goal is to reduce profile variance between runs and across runner implementations so that downstream model pinning and routing decisions are stable.
technical_notes:
- Implement reservoir+stratified sampler keyed by workload tags (chat, long-form, embed) and by token length buckets to match live traffic distributions.
- Introduce runner-level process isolation and per-run environment reset (CUDA cache clear, pinned RNG seeds, ephemeral temp directories).
- Add a compact run manifest (JSONL) with model version, seed, sampler snapshot, hardware profile, and kernel hints for traceability.
- Provide a runner shim API so legacy eval runners can opt into deterministic mode without full rewrite (shim toggles: deterministic_seed, env_reset=true, cache_mode=passthrough).
- Tradeoffs: stricter isolation increases runtime overhead and may reduce throughput; sampler stratification favours representativeness over random coverage; we will expose knobs to tune cost vs stability.
- Performance targets: reduce 95th percentile variance in token-rate benchmarks across repeated runs from current ~14% to <4% for pinned profiles on the same hardware tier.
acceptance_criteria: Sampler produces sample sets whose token-length and conversational-turn distributions match provided target profile within 5% L1 distance
Eval runners can run in deterministic mode with documented shim flags and pass the cross-run reproducibility check (identical manifest fields except run_id/timestamp)
Run manifests are persisted to the profile registry and used by the profile publisher during release; profiles with mismatched manifests are rejected
End-to-end test: generate profile for three different open models and verify per-token latency and memory metrics have <4% variance across 3 independent runs on identical hardware
comments: 2026-03-10 — Nadia Chen: Kickoff note. Met with PM and Research to align on target distributions. Agreed to start with chat/llm and embeddings workloads. Asked infra to reserve test cluster g4dn-like nodes for isolation experiments.

2026-03-11 — Ravi Kapoor: PoC sampler merged to feature branch. Reservoir stratification implementation exists, initial runs show better matching of length distribution but minor bias towards short sequences; adjusting bucket boundaries.
2026-03-11 — Design review (Maya Singh): Requested clearer UX for exposing 'deterministic mode' in harness docs and console. Suggest adding a toggle in the profile publisher UI and CLI description.

2026-03-12 — Engineering note: Implemented runner shim flags deterministic_seed and env_reset. Observed CUDA cache thrash causing 3-5% slower throughput in deterministic mode—documented tradeoff. Filing follow-up to evaluate lightweight cache reset vs full clear.

2026-03-12 — QA (Omar Li): Started reproducibility test matrix (models: open-llama-7b, vicuna-13b, embed-ada-like). First two runs show per-token latency variance 6% -> need to iterate on isolation steps.
2026-03-12 — PR feedback (reviewer @alvaro): Request to add telemetry tags (sampler_version, seed, runner_shim_version) to metric events so we can correlate regressions in console dashboards.
notes: Plan: 1) finish shim + sampler, 2) run reproducibility suite on reserved nodes, 3) iterate isolation strategy to reduce overhead, 4) publish manifest-aware profiles and update profile registry validation, 5) add console UX toggle and telemetry filter.

Risk: If deterministic isolation causes >10% throughput regression on common inference tiers, Dedicated customers may reject using pinned profiles. Mitigation: expose opt-in knobs and autoscaling recommendations in the profile publisher.
